provenance.author: HAND-LABELLED BY AN LLM (Claude, Opus 5), not by a human annotator and not by users
provenance.built_from: real entities taken from data/products.parquet (25,003 ESCI US products) - every brand and product phrase below occurs in the live catalogue
provenance.labelling_rule: gold_route = graph_local when answering requires traversing a relation BETWEEN catalogue items (substitute, complement, same-brand) starting from a named anchor; graph_global when the query asks for a theme across many items; hybrid when the query can be answered by ranking documents against the query text alone
limits: n=30. A 95% Wilson interval on a proportion measured on 30 items is roughly +/-0.15-0.20 wide, so precision/recall here cannot separate a good router from a mediocre one.

Single labeller, no adjudication, no inter-annotator agreement. The labeller also wrote the router rules, so the set is not independent of the system under test - it is a smoke test, not an unbiased benchmark.
Queries are written in clean English. Real Sparky traffic is short, misspelt and elliptical, which is the regime rules routers fail in.
The hybrid half is deliberately seeded with near-miss lexical traps ('substitute' as a food word, 'fits' as a size word) because those are the cases a keyword router gets wrong.

queries.query: cheaper alternative to the Keurig K-Mini single serve coffee maker
queries.justification: Needs an anchor item (Keurig K-Mini, a real catalogue product) and then a substitute relation plus a price comparison. Text ranking alone cannot express 'cheaper than this specific item'.

queries.query: something like the YETI Rambler 12 oz bottle but less expensive
queries.justification: Same shape as g01 with a different anchor (YETI Rambler, real product) and the paraphrase 'but less expensive' instead of 'cheaper'.

queries.query: I want a substitute for Garden of Life mykind Organic Men's multivitamin
queries.justification: 'substitute for <anchor>' is the substitute relation by name; the anchor is a real product with 58 ESCI substitute-supporting queries.

queries.query: budget replacement for the Chefman single serve coffee maker
queries.justification: 'replacement for' plus a price constraint over a named anchor: a substitute traversal, not a text match.

queries.query: what goes with the VEVOR dog grooming tub
queries.justification: Complement relation from a real anchor. ESCI labels 15 complement items around dog grooming tubs, so the edge exists in the data.

queries.query: accessories for the Anker portable charger
queries.justification: 'accessories for X' is a complement traversal; the answer is items related to the anchor, not items matching the anchor's text.

queries.query: what else do I need to use with a Booster Bath elevated pet bathing tub
queries.justification: Explicit complement intent ('what else do I need', 'use with') over a real anchor product.

queries.query: which storage bins pair with the mDesign closet organizer
queries.justification: 'pair with' is the complement phrase; requires linking mDesign (real brand, 63 products) then traversing.

queries.query: show me other baby clothes from the same brand as Simple Joys by Carter's rompers
queries.justification: Two hops: product -> brand -> other products of that brand. Simple Joys by Carter's is the second-largest brand in the catalogue (125 products).

queries.query: what else does Blue Buffalo make for dogs
queries.justification: Brand-node expansion. 'what else does X make' cannot be answered by ranking documents against the phrase itself.

queries.query: more from the same maker as the Nature Made vitamin D3 softgels
queries.justification: 'same maker' is the brand relation; the anchor names a real brand with 53 catalogue products.

queries.query: a cheaper alternative to Airheads candy variety bulk box
queries.justification: Highest-degree substitute anchor in the graph (62 supporting ESCI queries), so this query tests traversal on a dense node.

queries.query: what accessories work with the Safavieh area rug
queries.justification: 'work with' complement phrasing over a real brand (85 products). Included to test a complement query whose graph neighbourhood may be sparse - a legitimate miss is informative.

queries.query: summarise the common themes across Gerber baby food products
queries.justification: Asks for a cross-item summary, not a ranked list. This is the community-summary route in the playbook.

queries.query: overall what do shoppers buy alongside Keurig coffee makers in general
queries.justification: 'overall ... in general' signals global sense-making across a neighbourhood rather than a single-item lookup.

queries.query: gluten free pasta 16 oz
queries.justification: Pure attribute lookup. No relation between items is involved; hybrid retrieval is the correct and cheaper route.

queries.query: Hudson Baby cotton sleeper 0-3 months
queries.justification: Names a brand but asks for that brand's item directly - a product lookup, not a brand expansion. Tests that a brand mention alone does not trigger the graph.

queries.query: stainless steel water bottle with straw lid
queries.justification: Attribute-only query with no anchor entity and no relational verb.

queries.query: sugar substitute stevia packets
queries.justification: NEAR-MISS TRAP: contains the word 'substitute', but as part of the product's name ('sugar substitute'), not as a relational request. A keyword router that fires on 'substitute' is wrong here.

queries.query: car seat that fits a newborn
queries.justification: NEAR-MISS TRAP: 'fits' here is a size attribute of a single product, not a compatibility relation between two catalogue items.

queries.query: Nature Made vitamin D3 2000 IU softgels
queries.justification: Exact product lookup on the same brand used in g11, to check the router separates 'find this' from 'find more like this brand'.

queries.query: Blue Buffalo Life Protection chicken and rice dry dog food 30 lb
queries.justification: Fully specified product; the answer is a ranking, not a traversal. Pairs with g10 on the same brand.

queries.query: unscented baby wipes sensitive skin
queries.justification: Attribute query in the catalogue's largest eval category with no relational language.

queries.query: wireless charging pad for iphone
queries.justification: NEAR-MISS TRAP: 'for iphone' is compatibility language, but iPhone is not a catalogue item here, so there is no anchor node to traverse from and hybrid is correct. Tests the entity-linking guard, not just the regex.

queries.query: organic dark chocolate sea salt caramels
queries.justification: Descriptive product query matching a real catalogue item (Sanders) with no relational verb.

queries.query: 12 cup programmable coffee maker with timer
queries.justification: Feature query in the same product space as g01/g04, but with no anchor item, so it must stay on hybrid.

queries.query: mDesign bathroom storage bins clear plastic
queries.justification: Brand plus attributes, direct lookup. Pairs with g08 on the same brand to test the relational-verb requirement.

queries.query: probiotics for women 50 billion cfu
queries.justification: Dosage/attribute query in a dense health_household neighbourhood; relations are not needed to answer it.

queries.query: silicone spatula set heat resistant
queries.justification: Attribute query matching a real catalogue item (DI ORO) with no anchor-and-relation structure.

queries.query: YETI Rambler 12 oz bottle hot shot cap
queries.justification: Exact product lookup for the anchor used in g02. The only difference between the two is the relational phrase, which isolates what the router is actually keying on.
